title: Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of morphisms between qcqs schemes; finite presentation is stable under base change
statement: Let $f:U\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. (1) If $U$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is quasi-compact; if $U$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. In particular, if $U$ is affine, $T$ quasi-separated and $f$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] (for instance etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]), then $f$ is of finite presentation. (2) If $f$ is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) and $T$ is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated), then $U$ is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated). (3) The base change of a morphism locally of finite presentation (resp. quasi-compact, quasi-separated, of finite presentation) along any morphism is locally of finite presentation (resp. quasi-compact, quasi-separated, of finite presentation).
